title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page sits inside Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', a sequel to La Longue Marche. The 'loop equation' is a relation in a matrix group G (the neighbouring pages mention GL(2), GP(1) [presumably PGL(1)/projective group] and SL(2)). M_{ρ,σ} denotes an object (scheme or torsor-like) whose sections φ parametrise solutions attached to the data (ε_0, ρ, σ).

On the previous page (p.458), a section φ is described in two ways:
(i) by a triple (α, β, f);
(ii) by (U, a, b), with U ∈ G, a ∈ Γ T_ρ and b ∈ Γ N'_σ (T_ρ and T_0 are tori; N'_σ is presumably a normaliser-type subgroup), together with u related to det U.
The question raised there is: when does (α, β, γ) determine the section, and which conditions must it satisfy to come from one? Uniqueness holds under condition (164): T_0 ∩ T_ρ ∩ N'_σ = {1}.

On this page Grothendieck studies the action of an element f (implicitly in SG, since he uses det f = 1) by φ_1 = f^{-1} φ_0.
- In the (U, a, b) description: U_1 = f^{-1} U_0, a_1 = a_0, b_1 = b_0 (formula 166).
- Justification: Θ_G restricted to SG is the conjugation of SG in G, while Θ_ρ and Θ_σ are trivial on SG.
- Also u_1 = u_0, because det U_1 = det U_0.
- Hence in the (α, β, f) description: α_1 = α_0, β_1 = β_0, f_1 = f_0 f (formula 165).

So the f-component is acted on simply transitively by right translation, and the (α, β) components are invariants. Consequently the sought condition for (α, β, f) to come from a section depends only on (α, β). Geometrically, M_{ρ,σ} looks like an SG-torsor over its image in (α, β)-space.

He hopes this condition can be expressed as the validity of the explicit 'formule des bouts' (157), for a permutation ε with ε² = 1. He notes that the analysis of this condition is the subject of sections (II) and (III), with conditions more draconian than those imposed on the triple (ε_0, ρ, σ) in the preceding paragraph (p.531').

The diagonal left-margin note warns that the condition is not sufficient: there are exceptional cases, and one must additionally require u ∈ T_0. It also mentions a polynomial-type identity B = αctbd + bc (?) and B = 0. The note ends with something like '… ∈ M_{ρ,σ}(Q̄)' (reading uncertain), suggesting that he is thinking of points over Q̄.

The next page admits these conditions may be more restrictive than necessary and frames the GL(2)/SL(2) study as 'débroussage' for a more general context.
errors: Minor logical ordering: the text writes 'd'où (165)' after first stating (165) and then deriving (166). The intended logic is (166) + u_1 = u_0 ⇒ (165), which is consistent. The assumption det f = 1 (f ∈ SG) is used but not stated explicitly on the page.
The margin itself acknowledges that the hoped-for characterisation via (157) is not sufficient without the extra condition u ∈ T_0. The main text's hope is therefore incomplete as stated.

ideas.what: The SG-action φ ↦ f^{-1}φ on sections of M_{ρ,σ} fixes the (α,β) invariants and translates the f-component, so the existence condition depends only on (α,β).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor structure / quotient by a free group action; reduction of a moduli problem to invariants

ideas.what: Trying to characterise the image (which (α,β) come from solutions) by an explicit identity, the 'formule des bouts' (157), for an involution ε, with exceptional cases requiring u ∈ T_0.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit description of the image of a morphism of varieties of representations (matrix solutions of a loop equation)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the loop-equation discussions around La Longue Marche (1981), but the specific formulas are not published.

missed.claim: The characterisation of the (α,β) arising from sections of M_{ρ,σ} via formula (157) is left open. Grothendieck flags its insufficiency (exceptional cases, the need for u ∈ T_0) and on the next page says he may have to return to it in a more general setting than GL(2)/SL(2). This is a local technical loose end in the unpublished 'équation des lacets' programme rather than a standalone result.
missed.quote: On voudrait que elles s'expriment par la validité de la formule (157) explicite, pour une permutation ε ... (ε^2 = 1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as part of reconstructing the unpublished loop-equation programme (linked to the Teichmüller tower and Galois action). By itself it is a routine step.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine bookkeeping page: invariance of (α,β) under an SG-translation and a reduction of the existence problem to (α,β). No new construction or connection is visible beyond the general unpublished programme.
transcription_corrections: '(car Θ_G | SG = relation conjugue SG ou G' likely reads 'Θ_G|SG = relation conjuguée SG en G' (Θ_G restricted to SG is the conjugation of SG in G).
'f_1 = f_0 f' is consistent with the image (written f_1 = f_0 f), not f∘f.
'Θ_ρ {+Θ_σ+}' corresponds to Θ_ρ with Θ_σ written as an insertion above; the crossed-out word under it is illegible.
The left margin likely ends with '... ∈ M_{ρ,σ}(Q̄)' or similar; the reading is very uncertain. 'par. p. 4112'' is probably 'par. p. 411'' or 'p. 531''.
